title: Auction Bench
question: Can the agent bid well against other bidders?
blurb: Six items go up for auction at once, and bidding closes after 15 minutes of real time. The agent bids against four scripted rivals with a £1,000 budget and pays a small fee for every bid. Nobody can chat. Each model plays five auctions, and in each one the items are worth different amounts to each bidder.
footnote: Scores on the Economic Intelligence Index's 0-100 scale, rescaled from the benchmark's own results. The questions below explain the scale.

notes.measures: Knowing what things are worth and bidding with discipline: winning items for less than their value, spreading the budget, and leaving bidding wars that lose money.
notes.scoring: The raw result is the agent's profit: what the items it won are worth to it, minus what it paid and the fees. We compare it with what a bidder earns in the same auction by bidding exactly what each item is worth to it. 0 means no profit, and a loss also scores 0. 100 means matching that bidder; doing better still scores 100.
notes.original: We built Auction Bench. In pounds, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash made £152 per auction on average and Claude Opus 5.5 £144. Comparing each profit with that bidder's puts auctions with bigger and smaller prizes on one scale.
